method.name: bridgeHandshake
method.signature: bridgeHandshake(request: { kind: 'hello'; protocolVersion: 2; sessionNonce: string }): Promise<{ kind: 'ready'; protocolVersion: 2; sessionNonce: string }>;
method.purpose: The bridge-control protocol-2 startup wire exchange is exactly one UTF-8 NDJSON hello record {kind:'hello',protocolVersion:2,sessionNonce} from the client on helper stdin, then exactly one ready record {kind:'ready',protocolVersion:2,sessionNonce} on helper stdout. The client generates a fresh unpredictable sessionNonce per helper process; helper echoes it only after validating the version and binding its configured local installation endpoint. This is a separate startup envelope, not an IpcBridgeRequest and not a correlated controlBridge outcome; it has no transportId because no request exists yet. The helper must not forward any application frame before emitting ready, and the client must not send send/cancel records until matching ready is received. Set a 3-second handshake deadline from helper spawn; missing/malformed/duplicate/wrong-version/wrong-nonce ready, early outcome frames, or helper exit fail with bridge-protocol-mismatch/bridge-handshake-timeout before dispatch. On error the client closes stdin and that helper lane, reports no sends dispatched, and performs no automatic fallback/replay; it sends no daemon signal/stop. Unsupported hello yields only a bounded stderr diagnostic and helper exit without opening an application RPC lane. After ready, stdout contains only the specified correlated controlBridge events, stderr only diagnostics; later hello/ready records are protocol errors. Handshake bytes count toward the bounded parser/input limits; no credentials/capability tokens are echoed. Existing inner IpcBridgeRequest.protocolVersion=1 remains unchanged and is distinct from outer bridge-control version 2.

body.rationale: Complete pending controlBridge protocol-2 negotiation with an exact wire handshake, deadline and zero-dispatch failure semantics.
